repo_model.summary: This repository is a RelBench generic-search candidate workspace. The root candidate loads a task from the sanitized cache, emits task-family-specific validation and test prediction arrays, and is evaluated by the provided grader using official validation metrics.

entrypoints.how_to_run: From the repository root with the RelBench and output environment variables set: python main.py --debug for the fast build or python main.py for the full build.
Run python kapso_evaluation/grader.py --fidelity fast|full [--fraction F] [--seed S] with the handler-provided environment.

where_to_edit.role: Primary solution entrypoint; replace the trivial task-family prediction logic with data loading, feature construction, training, and prediction.
Reusable task-loading, output-saving, temporal-safety, and MAP@K helper functions.
Authoritative input/output and evaluation constraints to consult before changing the candidate.
Provided scoring infrastructure to inspect for protocol details; it is not the candidate implementation to modify.

claims.statement: The evaluation flow is split between an isolated child process running root main.py and a provided grader that loads the resulting prediction files, validates them, and computes official RelBench validation metrics.

evidence.description: The grader locates and runs the candidate main.py.
The candidate command is selected as python main.py, optionally with --debug.
Validation predictions are evaluated through the task's official evaluate method.

claims.statement: main.py reads dataset and task identity from environment variables, loads the RelBench task without downloading, and derives validation/test row counts from the task tables; an empty validation snapshot indicates rolling evaluation.

evidence.description: Dataset identity is read from RELBENCH_DATASET.
The task is loaded with download=False.
The code documents the empty-validation rolling snapshot behavior.
Test row count is obtained from the task table.

claims.statement: The seeded candidate chooses prediction shapes and values by task family: ranked integer IDs for recommendation, 0.5 probabilities for binary classification, uniform class scores for multiclass classification, and the training-target median for other task types.

evidence.description: Recommendation tasks use a dedicated prediction branch.
Recommendation rows are generated as integer ranges of length eval_k.
Binary classification uses a constant 0.5 prediction.
Multiclass classification uses a class-probability matrix.
Other tasks use the median of the training target.

claims.statement: kapso_datasets/common.py provides the intended higher-level integration layer: it loads dataset, task, database, and train/validation/test tables into TaskContext and supplies a contract-compliant prediction saver.

evidence.description: load_task is the helper for loading the sanitized dataset/task context.
The dataset database is loaded and the task tables are assembled.
save_predictions writes both prediction arrays.

claims.statement: For ordinary candidate runs, both val_predictions.npy and test_predictions.npy must exist after every run, and prediction rows must remain positionally aligned with the corresponding RelBench validation and test tables; validation predictions must be out-of-sample.

evidence.description: Both prediction files are required after every run.
Rows must align positionally with the task tables.
Validation predictions must come from a model that did not train on validation labels.

claims.statement: Required output formats are binary float vectors in [0,1], regression float vectors, multiclass float matrices with one column per class, and recommendation integer matrices of shape (N, K) containing ranked destination IDs.

evidence.description: Binary and regression prediction types and binary range are specified.
Multiclass and recommendation shapes/types and recommendation ID constraints are specified.
Recommendation shape and integer dtype are checked.
Non-recommendation prediction shapes are checked.

claims.statement: The search score is the official primary validation metric; test predictions are collected as artifacts but cannot be scored from the sanitized cache because test labels are absent.

evidence.description: The official validation primary metric is the search score.
Test labels are physically absent from the cache.
The manifest score is taken from the configured primary validation metric.

claims.statement: Dataset and task access must use the sanitized local cache with download=False; candidates must not probe for test labels.

evidence.description: The RelBench API must be used with download=False.
The cache is read-only and contains no test labels.
The dataset helper explicitly loads with download=False.

claims.statement: The required end-to-end sanity check is python main.py --debug, followed by the full run command python main.py; both runs are expected to produce contract-valid prediction artifacts.

evidence.description: The harness runs the debug invocation from the repository root.
The harness then runs the full invocation.

claims.statement: After writing predictions, run python kapso_datasets/check_predictions.py to catch missing files, shape mismatches, invalid dtypes, non-finite values, and binary range violations before scoring.

evidence.description: The contract recommends the prediction self-check command.
The checker validates both validation and test files.
Successful split checks and the all-checks-passed result are printed.

claims.statement: A fast grader dry run still scores the complete validation split and emits the machine-readable KAPSO_EVAL_MANIFEST containing the official score.

evidence.description: Fast fidelity runs main.py --debug.
The scored item set never shrinks.
The grader prints the machine-readable manifest line.

claims.statement: The seeded main.py is intentionally not a real solution: it emits constants or a training-median baseline, so replacing its prediction logic is necessary for meaningful performance.

evidence.description: The module is described as a baseline candidate.
The file explicitly instructs the user to replace it with a real solution.
Binary predictions are constant.
Regression-like predictions use only the training target median.

claims.statement: In rolling evaluation, an empty validation parquet causes main.py to treat the invocation as a tick and omit val_predictions.npy; the grader instead collects each tick's test_predictions.npy and assembles the official validation/test vectors.

evidence.description: Rolling snapshots are documented as having an empty validation table.
An absent or empty validation table produces n_val == 0 and rolling mode.
Validation output is skipped during rolling ticks.
The rolling grader requires test_predictions.npy for each tick.
Per-tick predictions are assembled into final split vectors.

claims.statement: The baseline recommendation branch always predicts IDs 0 through eval_k-1 without consulting num_dst_nodes, so some IDs can be outside the valid destination range and fail to match.

evidence.description: Recommendation IDs are generated as a fixed range based only on eval_k.
The checker warns when recommendation IDs are outside the valid destination range.

claims.statement: Fast fidelity only changes the candidate invocation to include --debug; scoring still uses the complete validation split, and fraction/seed do not subsample validation rows.

evidence.description: Fast fidelity invokes the candidate in debug mode.
The validation item set never shrinks.
Fraction and seed are only echoed into the manifest.

claims.statement: The runtime requires Python with relbench and numpy installed; the candidate directly imports NumPy and RelBench task APIs.

evidence.description: NumPy is imported by the candidate.
RelBench task classes and task loading are imported.
Configuration is supplied through environment variables.
The suite needs Python with relbench and numpy installed.

claims.statement: The handler supplies task identity, cache location, primary metric, timeouts, work/archive directories, and shared-cache configuration through environment variables; main.py additionally requires KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR for its output location.

evidence.description: The grader documents the required task, metric, work, timeout, and cache variables.
The shared candidate cache variable is documented.
The candidate requires RELBENCH_DATASET and RELBENCH_TASK.
The candidate reads RELBENCH_CACHE_DIR.
Prediction output is written under KAPSO_RUN_DATA_DIR.
